facts.balanced: The guide describes SCHNAIL (Starcraft Human and AI League) as a client with its own game installation and matchmaking. An initial login needs an internet connection.

facts.gentle: The guide rates SCHNAIL as the most realistic option; its drawback is an internet login.
facts.balanced: Pros listed: more realistic AI, better micro and macro, game integration, active community. Cons: internet needed for the first login; the AI then plays over the local network.

facts.gentle: The guide has a compatibility discrepancy: its prerequisites mention original or Remastered, but the setup section requires a separate Brood War 1.16.1 installation. Check the exact edition before proceeding.

facts.gentle: For Brood War 1.16.1, put BWAILauncher in the game directory and launch through it. If detection fails, check the path to Starcraft.exe.
facts.balanced: For Brood War 1.16.1, extract BWAILauncher into the game directory and run BWAILauncher.exe. In its settings, select Starcraft.exe if automatic detection fails; then save and restart.

facts.gentle: If BWAILauncher does not detect your Starcraft installation, the guide says to set the path to Starcraft.exe in the launcher settings.
facts.balanced: If BWAILauncher does not detect your Starcraft installation automatically: open its settings, go to the “Game” or “Paths” section, select your Starcraft.exe file, then save the settings and restart the launcher.

facts.gentle: The guide says BWAILauncher works with portable Starcraft installations.
facts.balanced: The guide says BWAILauncher works well with portable Starcraft installations: extract it into the portable Starcraft directory, point it to the Starcraft.exe in that directory, and settings stay in the same folder.

facts.gentle: BWAILauncher is the guide's offline option that replaces the standard single-player AI.
facts.balanced: The guide says BWAILauncher replaces the standard single-player AI and works offline. Its setup instructions target Brood War 1.16.1.

facts.gentle: The guide rates BWAILauncher as the easy offline option, with less realistic AI.

facts.gentle: The guide has a short tips list for BWAILauncher, including trying different difficulty settings.
facts.balanced: Tips listed: it replaces the standard AI so you can use it in single-player mode; the AI is more challenging than the default but has micro-management limitations; try different difficulty settings; and check the GitHub repository for updates and community support.

facts.gentle: The guide lists BWAILauncher as the option that needs no internet connection.
facts.balanced: The guide's BWAILauncher pros: no internet connection required, replaces the standard single-player AI, easier to set up initially, and good for offline play.

research.text: BWAPI is a free, open-source C++ framework for writing AI bots that play StarCraft: Brood War; its setup expects the game updated to version 1.16.1.
